_about: fak position rows for the 'distributed' group. dim_id links each to a _taxonomy.json dimension.

rows.axis: Prefill-decode disaggregation: independent scaling of compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode
rows.competitor: DistServe; Splitwise; SGLang-PD / vLLM disaggregated; llm-d (vLLM + NIXL KV connector)
rows.fak_doc: No P/D-disaggregation goodput/TTFT number in BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md or CLAIMS.md. fak runs a single fused forward (prefill+decode together); no disaggregated prefill/decode pool is built or measured.
rows.comparison_note: EXCLUDE / out-of-scope for fak-native's mid-market 1-8 GPU target. OUT OF SCOPE for the reuse kernel: fak does not disaggregate prefill from decode into independently-scaled pools; its differentiator is cross-agent prefix fusion on one kernel, not P/D separation. DistServe/Splitwise/SGLang-PD/llm-d numbers have no fak counterpart; named as out-of-scope rather than a measured gap.

rows.competitor: NVIDIA Dynamo; DistServe; llm-d; DeepSeek (production PD-disagg)
rows.fak_doc: No prefill-decode disaggregation is shipped or claimed. fak's own engine runs a single co-located forward; on the GPU server it fronts SGLang TP=8 (which itself is not run in a disaggregated config in the committed GPU server artifacts).
rows.comparison_note: EXCLUDE / out-of-scope for fak-native's mid-market 1-8 GPU target. OUT OF SCOPE for a reuse kernel. PD-disaggregation with per-phase SLO isolation (DistServe 7.4x request rate / 12.6x tighter SLO; NVIDIA Dynamo Planner) is a serving-stack architecture; fak owns neither the prefill/decode scheduler nor the per-phase GPU pools. It is an adjudication/coherence plane that rides on whatever engine does this. no-claim.

rows.axis: Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) for giant MoE models
rows.fak_doc: none — fak runs GLM-5.2 MoE experts on ONE datacenter GPU (CLAIMS Engine, commit 498a4ab), never EP across nodes
rows.comparison_note: EXCLUDE / out-of-scope for fak-native's mid-market 1-8 GPU target. OUT OF SCOPE for a single-box reuse kernel. fak DOES run Inkling-2-Mini (26B hybrid MoE) on single consumer CUDA GPUs (RTX 5080), Qwen3.8-27B BF16 TP2 / Q4_K_M, and GLM-5.2 MoE/FFN experts + router on pure k_q8_gemm CUDA kernels (commit 498a4ab, 1 datacenter GPU, sparse DSA attention host-side), with no cross-node EP sharding; frontier 671B-1T giant-MoE EP is delegated to fronted SGLang/DeepEP. Verdict no-claim.

OUT OF SCOPE for a single-device reuse kernel. DP attention is a multi-device memory-deduplication technique (eliminate KV duplication across GPUs); fak runs one in-kernel KV cache on one device and has no hybrid attention/FFN parallelism. fak's KV story is prefix-REUSE across agents on one cache (RadixAttention parity, kv-hit-rate row), an orthogonal axis from DP-attention's cross-device dedup. No fak number; verdict no-claim.

rows.axis: Multi-node scale-out (combined TP x PP x EP x DP across hosts)
rows.competitor: SGLang; NVIDIA Dynamo; TensorRT-LLM; NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72
rows.fak_doc: none — fak's own engine is single-box (CLAIMS GPU backends are all one device); the 8-GPU datacenter server run is SGLang-serves + fak-adjudicates
rows.comparison_note: EXCLUDE / out-of-scope for fak-native's mid-market 1-8 GPU target. fak's native engine targets single-node 1-2 GPU local execution (CPU, RTX 5080/5090 Laptop, AMD RX 7600, Apple M3 Pro, datacenter GPU TP2), rather than multi-node 72-288 GPU NVLink/InfiniBand clusters. When fronting multi-GPU SGLang on an 8-GPU datacenter server, fak acts as the gateway/adjudication plane and trails raw SGLang on throughput. Verdict no-claim.
